item.title: Watchdog group warns Pittsburgh high school course recruits students into political activism
item.description: The North American Values Institute claims Pittsburgh Public Schools' ethnic studies course teaches political activism, not history, citing units on challenging systems of power.
item.content:encoded:
As the school year kicks off, education is under the microscope, with parents and organizations scrutinizing curricula. Now, the North American Values Institute (NAVI), a nonpartisan education watchdog, is sounding the alarm over Pittsburgh Public Schools' (PPS) new ethnic studies course for high school seniors. The organization claims that rather than focusing on teaching students history, the course appears to be a how-to guide for political activism.

"I have a simple philosophy: Teach kids about revolutions, don't recruit them to be in one," NAVI Pennsylvania Director Steve Rosenberg told Fox News Digital.

Referring to PPS documents that NAVI obtained through right-to-know requests, Rosenberg expressed concerns over how the school was planning to approach the course topic and the lack of counterarguments in provided class materials. NAVI sent the documents to Fox News Digital.

CONTROVERSIAL TEACHER TRAINING TARGETS PARENTAL AUTHORITY AS OPPRESSION, EDUCATION EXPERT WARNS

When asked to confirm if the documents were in fact accurate and current, Dr. Ann Fillmore, executive director K-12 Literacy, Humanities and Library Services for Pittsburgh Public Schools, said in a statement, "We provided the organization unit overview — not full curriculum. Some of the documents included, are individual course syllabi created by teachers."

Fillmore also noted that some of the individual teacher syllabi were specifically for a College in High School (CHS) dual-enrollment course affiliated with LaRoche University, rather than curriculum written by the district. 

"In addition, the CHS [College in High School] course syllabus are [sic] included and that course is not created through Pittsburgh Public Schools C&I [Office of Curriculum & Instruction]," Fillmore said, adding that the district's unit overviews have been revised for the 2026–2027 school year.

According to district documents, the course is divided into five units:

Each unit is set to be taught over the course of several weeks. The first two units of the course lay the foundational groundwork, focusing on identity formation, cultural heritage and historical migration. NAVI's concerns are primarily focused on the latter half of the course, starting with Unit 3.

BLISTERING REPORT EXPOSES HOW NATIONAL K-12 GROUP'S DEI AGENDA IS TRICKLING DOWN TO LOCAL SCHOOLS

In Unit 3, students are asked to explore how systems of power are built and how they can "challenge, resist and restructure" those systems in order to make them "equitable for all." The learning outcomes for Unit 3 include explaining "how systems of power give privilege to specific groups of people," discussions on how those systems "develop inequities," and examining "strategies of marginalized communities and groups to shift power dynamics within societies and articulate visions of alternative social systems."

Meanwhile, in Unit 4, students are asked to explore the limiting factors of systems of power, such as how they can impact access to opportunities and resources and how people make "choices about their lives." The learning outcomes include having students "develop and propose strategies to advocate for change within social systems that create inequitable outcomes for different ethnic groups."

"Those are very different from just learning about what people have gone through and [their] journey through this country," Rosenberg said of the third and fourth units.

In Unit 5, students are instructed to take what they have learned and put it into action. The learning objectives state that students are to "develop an action plan, including a clear problem, goal, and steps" and to "develop and communicate solutions to community issues relating to race and diversity." The students are instructed to work on their plan with others within the school or the community.

FAR-LEFT ACTIVIST CONFERENCE AT TEACHERS UNION HQ RAISES CLASSROOM CONCERNS

In the statement provided to Fox News Digital, Fillmore refuted NAVI's characterization of the course, calling it "inaccurate" and emphasizing that the curriculum is designed to teach civic reasoning, not political activism.

"We don’t train students — it is disrespectful to what the education institution is — we want them to develop their own original ideas, understandings of history, and solutions to problems, based on the principles of inquiry-based learning and National Council for the Social Studies (NCSS) College, Career, and Civic Life (C3) Framework," Fillmore's statement read.

Addressing units 3 and 4, Fillmore said that they are grounded in the National Council for the Social Studies (NCSS) C3 Framework and are meant to "promote engaged and active citizenship by helping students identify community issues, investigate them through research, evaluate potential responses, and consider how communities work together to address challenges."

NAVI's concerns go beyond the debate over political activism, with the group objecting to how the course addresses Jewish identity and antisemitism. Unit 1 of the CHS syllabus includes readings on Whiteness and privilege, as well as Eric Goldstein's "The Price of Whiteness: Jews, Race, and American Identity." Rosenberg argued that filtering Jewish identity through theories of privilege misrepresents the Jewish experience.

"There is no counter reading to that, that would show that Jews have been one of the two most oppressed people probably in the history of this country, in every country that the Jews have ever been, kicked out everywhere they've ever been," Rosenberg told Fox News Digital. "So, just to show because this one person that wrote this book or the teacher that's teaching this curriculum thinks that Jews are the oppressor is not OK. They can have that opinion, but show a second, a counter narrative, so that you can take the material to the students, read both, and then make their own determination."

However, Fillmore rejected the claim, saying that the course does not characterize specific groups as "oppressor" or "oppressed."

"Ethnic Studies intentionally avoids reducing individuals or groups to simplistic categories such as 'oppressor' and 'oppressed' because history, identity, and lived experiences are far more complex," Fillmore said.

"Jewish history, culture, resilience, and contributions are embedded throughout the curriculum. Students learn about the long-standing presence and experiences of Jewish Americans, including the challenges they have faced and the ways Jewish communities have preserved identity, culture, and collective memory across generations," Fillmore added, noting Pittsburgh's local connection with antisemitism after the 2018 attack at the Tree of Life synagogue.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE COVERAGE OF MEDIA AND CULTURE

Fillmore also disagreed with NAVI's concerns about the curriculum not presenting counter narratives, saying that it "does not reflect how the course is designed or taught." She noted that a "core principle of the course is inquiry-based learning" and that teachers pull from several sources, including primary and secondary sources, oral histories, literature and more when facilitating discussions.

For Rosenberg and NAVI, the central concern about how the schools will handle the course remains, particularly when it comes to the perspectives included in the class. He argues that students may not feel comfortable raising counterpoints of view.

"If the teacher who's standing up in front of the room is telling you this is the way it is, it is very hard for young people to have a counter-narrative, to have any kind of other opinion, because they're afraid they're going to not get a good grade, or they are going to be bias against them from other people," Rosenberg told Fox News Digital.

Rosenberg is urging parents to be thorough and go through course materials. He said parents need "to know how to ask the right questions" when it comes to what their children are hearing in the classroom.

item.title: Elon Musk lands new Trump administration role shaping future of American warfare
item.description: Elon Musk will co-lead Project Meridian with Palmer Luckey and Newt Gingrich to map future warfare domains and military technologies for the Pentagon.
item.content:encoded:
Elon Musk is taking on a new role in the Trump administration, this time helping the Pentagon determine which weapons and technology American troops will need to fight the wars of the future.

War Secretary Pete Hegseth announced Wednesday that Musk will co-lead Project Meridian, a new Pentagon initiative tasked with looking years and even decades ahead to identify emerging domains of warfare and the capabilities the U.S. military will need to dominate them.

Musk, the former leader of the Trump administration's Department of Government Efficiency (DOGE), will lead the effort alongside defense tech billionaire Palmer Luckey and former House Speaker Newt Gingrich under the direction of War Department Chief Technology Officer Emil Michael.

EXCLUSIVE: HEGSETH TO DOUBLE CUTS TO GENERALS, ADMIRALS IN MAJOR PENTAGON SHAKEUP

"The best forecasters of future conflict do not solely reside inside the Pentagon," Hegseth said during his State of the Force address at Marine Corps Base Quantico. "There are obvious biases and risks to asking ourselves to both ask the questions and answer them."

Hegseth said the initiative would begin immediately, and he would meet with Musk, Luckey and Gingrich in a secure site just 200 yards from the stage after his speech.

Project Meridian will have 120 days to "ruthlessly map the trajectory of wars, domains and technologies," culminating in a public rollout of its findings and a classified annex.

Hegseth described a sweeping mandate that stretches "from under the Earth to beyond the moon." 

Rather than developing new military strategies or policies, the group will seek to identify "the domains that we must conquer and capabilities we must master" and focus on "discovering, developing and fielding" weapons and systems that could be needed by future generations of American troops.

Musk and Luckey enter the effort with firsthand experience developing technology for the U.S. military. Musk's SpaceX is a major Pentagon contractor, while Luckey founded Anduril Industries, a defense technology company specializing in autonomous weapons and other advanced military systems.

Their industry experience positions both men to bring an unusually close view of emerging technology and the modern battlefield to the Pentagon's long-range planning. It could also raise potential conflict-of-interest questions as executives whose companies compete for defense business help identify the capabilities and technologies the military should pursue.

BATTLEFIELD ROBOTS OPEN NEW FRONT IN INNOVATION WAR WITH MAJOR US ADVERSARY

Meridian was one piece of a broader push announced by Hegseth Wednesday to remake the military around autonomous warfare and rapidly emerging technology.

Hegseth announced the creation of Autonomous Warfare Command, or AUTOWARCOM, a new four-star combatant command with what he described as "service-like authorities" to scale autonomous and robotic capabilities across the joint force.

The War Department will also begin phasing in new occupational frameworks across the military departments to create dedicated career paths for what Hegseth called a new generation of "autonomous warfighters."

"We should have been thinking about Autonomous Warfare Command ten years ago," Hegseth said, explaining that Meridian is intended to look far enough ahead to anticipate the next technological transformation before the military falls behind.

The announcements came during the second iteration of what the War Department has dubbed Hegseth’s annual State of the Force address at Marine Corps Base Quantico.

The setting was the same as last year, but the audience was markedly different. Hegseth summoned generals, admirals and other senior military leaders from around the world to Quantico for his first address, where he laid out sweeping changes to military standards, personnel and what he called the "warrior ethos."

This time, Hegseth addressed a younger generation of military leaders, including top-performing E-6 enlisted service members and O-3 officers from across the force. He called them the military’s "current and future leaders on the front lines" and said the address would become an annual opportunity to assess the state of the force and lay out his vision for its future.

Hegseth used Wednesday’s speech to unveil six new initiatives, ranging from the military’s embrace of autonomous warfare to an effort to make U.S. bases and defense supply chains less vulnerable to foreign disruption.

The secretary also used the address to deliver some of his most pointed rhetoric yet about his effort to reshape the culture of the military and about the news media.

"We are no longer the woke department or the weak department," Hegseth said. "No fatties, no trainees, no weirdos, no beardos, no wimps, no radicals. Just warriors."

Hegseth later accused some journalists of engaging in "partisan activism" that jeopardizes military operations and service members, calling such reporting "fundamentally anti-American."

"It’s sick. It’s a national betrayal. It’s treason, actually," Hegseth said.

item.title: Anne Hathaway takes charge at the 'Verity' red carpet in viral moment
item.description: Anne Hathaway's viral red carpet video shows her directing photographers during the "Verity" premiere while debuting her baby bump in Prabal Gurung.
item.content:encoded:
Anne Hathaway took control of the red carpet while at the premiere of her latest film.

While posing with the cast of her new film, "Verity," the 43-year-old actress calmly instructed photographers on how she planned on posing for their photos, in order to get the best shot possible.

In videos from the red carpet, Hathaway is heard telling the photographers where she will be looking and when, and tells the whole cast to follow suit.

The video from the premiere went viral on social media, with many fans praising her ability to get the photo taken efficiently.

ANNE HATHAWAY, DAKOTA JOHNSON AND JOSH HARTNETT STAR IN R-RATED THRILLER ‘VERITY,’ OUT OCT 2

"Anne saw the group photo drifting and took the wheel immediately," one X user wrote, while another added, "She really said fine ill do it myself and honestly thats the energy every group photo needs."

Another fan took to the comments section on Facebook, writing, "Queen of Genovia knows best," with a fourth fan adding, "She's like "this dress and my ankles have a TIME LIMIT. let's make this EFFICIENT!!!"

Hathaway showed off her baby bump in a figure-hugging black mermaid gown designed by Prabal Gurung, which featured sequins, beading and a long sheer cape.

WATCH: Anne Hathaway directed photographers at the red carpet premiere of 'Verity'

This isn't the first time Hathaway has been recorded telling photographers what to do. A video of her greeting fans and paparazzi outside Valentino's fall 2022 show in Italy by telling them to "calma" went viral and became an audio trend, something Hathaway didn't expect.

GET ENTERTAINMENT SCOOP DELIVERED RIGHT TO YOUR EMAIL BY CLICKING HERE

LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS

"I remember that particular time, we were coming out of the pandemic so we were all feeling a little fragile," she told W Magazine in February 2024 about the viral video. "Like I said, so many of my fans learned about me when they were children. So their excitement comes from a pure place. I want them to know, I’m excited too. I feel like, if we can be calm in meeting each other, we’ll both be able to connect that much more significantly."

Hathaway is currently pregnant with her third child with her husband, Adam Shulman. The two tied the knot in September 2012 and share two sons; Jonathan and Jack.

The "Princess Diaries" star announced her third pregnancy on Instagram, in June, and debuted her baby bump on the red carpet at the world premiere of "The Odyssey" in London, England in July.

Her latest film, "Verity," which she stars in alongside Dakota Johnson and Josh Hartnett, is the fifth feature film the actress starred in this year. Her other films this year include "The End of Oak Street," "The Devil Wears Prada 2," "The Odyssey" and "Mother Mary."

PUT YOUR ENTERTAINMENT KNOWLEDGE TO THE TEST AND SEE HOW YOU SCORE

"It’s exciting, but it’s not like I planned it this way," she told The New Indian Express in August. "The five films are the proceeds of more than three years of work. It just so happens they are all out this year. Years ago, I would probably have been pretty stressed about that, but now I’m not. It’s fun to be here talking about films that I am so proud of."

item.title: Howard Stern warns ABC will have 'hell to pay' if something 'goes wrong' with Jimmy Kimmel's show
item.description: Radio host Howard Stern warned Tuesday that ABC would have "hell to pay" should anything "go wrong" with "Jimmy Kimmel Live!" while appearing as a guest on the late-night show.
item.content:encoded:
Radio host Howard Stern told the "Jimmy Kimmel Live!" audience Tuesday that ABC would have "hell to pay" if something went wrong with late-night host Jimmy Kimmel's show.

"I want to say something to ABC if they're watching right now," Stern said, noting he had previously heard rumors about the show and did not know what was true. "There is no man more loyal to this company than this guy.

"And what I mean by that, this is the truth. For years, I've said to him, you know, he goes to these things. ABC has a corporate function where they try to attract advertisers. Every year, he'd go to what they call the upfronts."

The radio host told the audience that Kimmel would always attend the events because ABC needed him to be there.

BOB IGER BREAKS SILENCE ON DISNEY'S SUSPENSION OF JIMMY KIMMEL OVER CHARLIE KIRK ASSASSINATION COMMENTS

"He has done everything for the company. And I hope that they keep that in mind," he said. "Oh my God. I don't know about you, but if something goes wrong, oh, is ABC going to have hell to pay. Am I correct? Are you with me?"

ABC did not immediately respond to Fox News Digital's request for comment.

Reports of Kimmel's show being canceled were dismissed by ABC earlier this month. A spokesperson pushed back on Page Six's report that Kimmel's contract would not be renewed, calling any reports about the future of the late-night show "speculative."

KIMMEL REVEALS HE'S INTERVIEWING JAMES TALARICO UNDER 'UNUSUAL CIRCUMSTANCES,' CITING FCC THREATS

"Howard Stern's reign as king of all media is over in more ways than one," Hollywood in Toto founder Christian Toto told Fox News Digital in a statement about Stern's remarks. "The man who once stood tall for free speech went silent during the woke culture wars. Now, he's rushing to a multi-millionaire's defense, someone whose show is likely costing ABC dearly.

"That explains why the network needs a drastic budget reduction to keep ‘Jimmy Kimmel Live!’ on the air," he continued. "If CBS was losing $40 million a year to keep Stephen Colbert employed, imagine what ABC must swallow to appease Kimmel.

"The old Stern would have recognized those basic business principles," Toto added. "The new version? He's an ultra-rich liberal supporting a fellow ultra-rich liberal while misleading the public on the issues in play."

Kimmel's show was taken off-air briefly in September 2025 after remarks the late-night host made about Charlie Kirk's assassin.

The liberal late-night personality returned to air a few days later and has referenced the suspension in frequent jabs directed at President Donald Trump, as well as Federal Communications Commission (FCC) chair Brendan Carr.

Kimmel, after returning from his summer break on Sept. 8, jabbed at Carr and said, "We're still here."

The late-night host noted that it was the 4,000th episode of "Jimmy Kimmel Live!"

"We’ve done 4,000 of these. Which is, it’s a lot of shows," Kimmel said. "According to the White House, it’s too many shows.

"There are those who said we would never last this long. There are even those who used the regulatory might of the FCC to unconstitutionally try to make sure we didn’t last this long. But we did it the hard way, Brendan. And we are still here."

DISNEY SUES FCC OVER ‘RETALIATORY CAMPAIGN AGAINST ABC,’ SEEKS TO BLOCK EARLY RENEWAL PROCEEDINGS

The late-night host had New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani on the show Monday night and questioned him repeatedly about the nature of his relationship with Trump.

The democratic socialist mayor seemed to deflect Kimmel's questions as Mamdani avoided criticizing Trump and rejected the late-night host's request to send him a selfie.

"Did you guys hit it off immediately or is it something that you really went into thinking, like, ‘OK, I need to have a relationship with the president of the United States, and I think the best way to do it is to charm him?' How did you do that and can you help me?" Kimmel asked Mamdani, calling his relationship with Trump "unexpected."

Mamdani responded, "Sorry, brother."

"The No. 1 thing that we've been speaking about recently has been Sunnyside Yard, which is this idea for decades of building a platform over a rail yard and then building 12,000 homes. And so, in that moment, you know, that you zoomed in on, I'm just thinking about 12,000 homes, 30,000 jobs, largest housing development since the early 1970s," Mamdani told Kimmel.

Kimmel asked, "When you text him about Sunnyside, are you sure he doesn't think you're texting him about eggs?"

Mamdani said he was "pretty sure" and noted that the texts were pretty normal and didn't resemble the president's Truth Social posts.

"Wow. You really have broken through with him," Kimmel said. "I mean, listen, you seem to be doing a great job in New York. We might need you to move to Washington just hang out at the Oval Office all day. Like, if you texted him a selfie of us right now."

MAMDANI SAYS EVEN IF HE CAN GET ALONG WITH TRUMP, HE STILL DEMANDS THAT 'ICE SHOULD BE ABOLISHED'

Mamdani laughed and shut it down.

"I love you, but I love housing more," Mamdani responded.

item.title: South Carolina mom accused of knife attack on young children; 6-year-old may lose arm: sheriff's office
item.description: Taylor Gosnell allegedly stabbed her two children approximately 50 times in their South Carolina home before her 6-year-old called his grandmother.
item.content:encoded:
A South Carolina boy’s call to his grandmother saying he was hungry led authorities to a home where investigators say his mother had stabbed him and his younger sibling dozens of times, leaving both children with severe injuries.

Taylor Gosnell, 35, was charged with two counts of attempted murder after allegedly attacking her children, ages 6 and 3, inside their Spartanburg County home during the overnight hours before they were discovered Saturday, according to authorities.

The 6-year-old called his grandmother Sept. 26, and told her his mother was not home and that he and his 3-year-old sibling were hungry, according to the Spartanburg County Sheriff’s Office.

ACCUSED NC KILLER MOM PLANS INSANITY DEFENSE — AS RETIRED JUDGE SAYS MORE MAY FOLLOW LINDSAY CLANCY STRATEGY

The grandmother contacted a friend of Gosnell, and the two went to the residence. They found both children suffering from severe injuries and immediately dialed 911.

Deputies responding shortly after 2:30 p.m. found the residence in disarray, with numerous items damaged or broken, authorities said.

Investigators said the children had approximately 50 stab wounds between them, including injuries that penetrated to the bone. Both were initially taken to Spartanburg Regional Medical Center before being transferred to Prisma Health Children’s Hospital in Greenville, where they remained hospitalized and were expected to undergo additional surgeries.

SUBURBAN ILLINOIS BOY DIES IN SUSPECTED DOMESTIC HOMICIDE AS NEIGHBORS FEAR ANOTHER LINDSAY CLANCY CASE

Arrest warrants reviewed by Fox News Digital provide additional details about the alleged attack. The warrants allege Gosnell struck the children with a baseball bat and a circular knife, causing severe injuries with intent to kill them.

Gosnell returned to the home while deputies were still there, according to the sheriff’s office. Deputies transported her to Spartanburg Regional Medical Center for an evaluation after observing behavior that raised concerns about her immediate well-being.

Authorities said Gosnell attempted to run from the ambulance before being transported and had to be restrained. She was medically cleared and released from the hospital shortly afterward.

DAYS AFTER LINDSAY CLANCY MISTRIAL, ANOTHER MASSACHUSETTS MOM ACCUSED OF KILLING HER CHILDREN SEEKS FREEDOM

Investigators attempted to interview Gosnell, but no interview was conducted after she requested an attorney, according to the sheriff’s office.

Gosnell was booked into the Spartanburg County Detention Facility shortly before midnight Sept. 26 and was denied bond on both attempted murder charges.

Investigators later obtained two additional warrants charging Gosnell with possession of a weapon during a violent crime. Those warrants, also reviewed by Fox News Digital, allege she possessed the weapons during the attempted murders.

The children have been placed in protective custody and remain hospitalized, authorities said.

The investigation remains active and ongoing.

item.title: 'The Five' leads cable news for 20th straight quarter as Fox News outdraws CNN and MS NOW combined
item.description: "The Five" marked its 20th consecutive quarter as cable news' top show while Fox News Channel outdrew both MS NOW and CNN combined.
item.content:encoded:
Fox News Channel continued to dominate ahead of its 30th anniversary, finishing the third quarter of 2026 ahead of CBS among weekday primetime viewers while crushing all of cable.

Fox News averaged 2.4 million weekday primetime viewers to beat CBS for the quarter while continuing to lead the broadcast network year-to-date among weekday primetime viewers.

When it comes to cable, Fox News averaged 1.3 million total-day viewers to finish as the only network to crack the one-million viewer benchmark. MS NOW finished second with an average audience of 592,000 followed by ESPN, CNN and HGTV.

FIRST LADY MELANIA TRUMP, FOX CORPORATION ANNOUNCE LANDMARK STRATEGIC ALLIANCE TO GROW FOSTERING THE FUTURE

During primetime, Fox News averaged 2.1 million viewers compared to 1.1 million for second-place ESPN. MS NOW settled for 930,000 and CNN managed only 607,000 as Fox News outdrew them combined in both categories.

Along the way, Fox News commanded 56% of the audience in total day and 57% during primetime.

"The Five," with Dana Perino, Greg Gutfeld, Jesse Watters, Emily Compagno, Jessica Tarlov and Harold Ford Jr., averaged 3.1 million viewers to finish as the No. 1 show on cable news. It was the 20th consecutive quarter that "The Five" has been the highest-rated show in cable news.

"Jesse Watters Primetime," "Gutfeld!," "Special Report with Bret Baier," "Hannity" and "The Ingraham Angle" rounded out the top six as Fox News offerings nearly swept the top 14 cable news programs. Fox News is on pace for its highest-rated midterm election year in network history with total day viewership.

The only non-Fox News program to finish inside the top 14 was MS NOW’s "The Rachel Maddow Show," which only airs once per week. "Maddow" averaged 1.9 million viewers to finish seventh, but only aired 10 episodes the entire quarter compared to 59 for "The Five."

CNN’s most-watched show was "Newsnight," which averaged 686,000 viewers to finish No. 24 among cable news programs.

"America’s Newsroom with Bill Hemmer and Dana Perino," "The Faulkner Focus," "Outnumbered," "America Reports with Sandra Smith and John Roberts," Martha MacCallum’s "The Story" and "The Will Cain Show" all had strong quarters as Fox News’ daytime lineup added to the network’s overwhelming success.

FOX NEWS DIGITAL THUMPS ALL NEWS BRANDS, INCLUDING BROADCAST NETWORKS, IN KEY PERFORMANCE INDICATORS DURING JULY

"Fox News @ Night with Trace Gallagher" averaged 1.3 million viewers to lead its timeslot, and "Gutfeld!" beat all broadcast and late-night television, including ABC’s "Jimmy Kimmel Live!" and NBC’s "The Tonight Show starring Jimmy Fallon."

"FOX & Friends" remained the most-watched morning show in cable news throughout the quarter with 1.1 million viewers, beating "CBS Mornings" in 21 markets, including New York, Philadelphia, Atlanta and Washington, D.C.

"FOX News Saturday Night with Jimmy Failla," "The Big Weekend Show," "My View with Lara Trump," "Life, Liberty & Levin," "The Sunday Briefing," hosted by rotating anchors Peter Doocy and Jacqui Heinrich, "Sunday Night in America with Trey Gowdy" and "One Nation with Brian Kilmeade" all thrived as Fox News continued to shine on weekends.

"Saturday in America with Kayleigh McEnany" was the most-watched cable news show on Saturdays with 1.4 million viewers, while "Sunday Morning Futures" averaged 1.4 million viewers to take the Sunday title.

Fox News also led cable news in the quarter among the advertiser-coveted demo of adults age 25-54, averaging 120,000 total day demo viewers and 183,000 during primetime. "The Five" averaged 289,000 to finish as the No. 1 show in the critical category.

item.title: Stewart expects Schumer, Jeffries to disappoint if the Dems win back the House and Senate
item.description: Jon Stewart warns Hakeem Jeffries and Schumer must deliver urgent economic results if Democrats win a historic midterm victory this November.
item.content:encoded:
Talk show host Jon Stewart suggested that even if Democrats win a massive victory in the midterms, a future Senate Majority Leader Chuck Schumer, D-N.Y., and a future Speaker of the House Hakeem Jeffries, D-N.Y., will turn out to be massive disappointments.

Democrats were initially in disarray after President Donald Trump’s victory against Kamala Harris in November. However, as Trump’s base fractured amid the Iran war and the affordability crisis that followed, Democrats are expected to win a historic victory in this November’s midterms.

On Wednesday, Stewart was asked a humorous question on his podcast about whether the downside of a Democratic midterm victory will be Schumer and Jeffries getting more "airtime."

"Look, I think what’s going to happen is they’re going to have to f---ing do something. They’re going to have to deliver," he said. "They’re not going to be able — it will not be sufficient to make their entire personalities opposition to whatever Trump politics are; they’re going to have to have a prescription for rebalancing this economy in a smart and urgent way.

JOHNSON DOWNPLAYS GOP'S MIDTERM WOES AS DEMOCRATS EYE HOUSE TAKEOVER: 'I AM VERY BULLISH'

"I am not confident that is in their DNA," Stewart continued. "I’m not confident that it’s in Schumer’s DNA, certainly, which means I’m actually hopeful he won’t be there as the leader. That they will come in and say, ‘We’re not going to go down that corporatist path again. We are going to make the changes that the American people are demanding that we make in an urgent way that is not bound by some idealized vision of what the parliamentarian might think is OK.’"

"F--- that," Stewart said. "Like, if you are granted control, if they give you the ring, do something with it, you b-----ds."

Fox News Digital contacted Jeffries and Schumer and did not receive an immediate reply.

HAKEEM JEFFRIES REJECTS MEDICARE FOR ALL, DSA AGENDA AS RO KHANNA CALLS HEALTH PLAN 'MOST IMPORTANT PRIORITY'

CLICK HERE FOR MORE COVERAGE OF MEDIA AND CULTURE

Veteran GOP strategist Mary Marslender told Fox News Digital she agrees with Stewart's take.

"I agree with Jon Stewart that both Schumer and Jeffries are not confident leaders, but that’s because their ideology is power," she responded. "They are not the brakes that will restrain the Democratic Party from pursuing a radical agenda. Instead, they often appease the more radical members of their conference and push the party leftwards on issues like the courts, federal agencies, government spending, progressive prosecutors and immigration whenever they have the votes.

"Both men have shown little willingness to challenge the party’s more extreme factions; for example, they have said they will welcome DSA candidates who win primaries into their ‘big tent’ party," she added. "They are not centrists; they follow the prevailing political winds within their party and will implement those policies to hold power even if those policies run counter to what the American people support."

Former Democratic advisor Dan Turrentine argued that Stewart's comments express the frustration Democratic voters have with party leaders.

"Voters are frustrated and angry that neither party is focused on them," he told Fox News Digital. "We are winning because Republicans are losing, not because we are doing things well. The D ‘Majority Makers’ are not going to be the progressive, base candidates, but moderates who will want to focus on commonsense affordability issues, not the 'revenge' and ‘blow everything up’ base stuff. 

"Jeffries and Schumer will need to balance this to protect their majority while maintaining base enthusiasm. It is a ‘both’ and not ‘either/or’ scenario. Given how weak both are, and that they both will face a primary challenge next year, it is going to be tough.

"I think Stewart is indicative of the irrational expectations of the base. They don’t appreciate the different reasons different people are angry. We are not potentially winning in Iowa, Arkansas, Kansas, Texas and South Carolina for the same reasons DSA candidates are winning."

item.title: Inside Diddy's prison life with massages, booze and nude photos: report
item.description: Sean "Diddy" Combs reportedly hired fellow inmates at Fort Dix to cook, clean and give massages, turning his prison unit into a luxury staffed operation.
item.content:encoded:
Sean "Diddy" Combs may be behind bars, but he has reportedly found a way to bring the perks of his former luxury lifestyle with him.

Combs, who is serving out his 50-month sentence at Fort Dix in New Jersey, has essentially hired a full staff within the prison walls, NBC News reported. Four men living in the same unit as the disgraced music mogul spoke to the outlet about the unusual comforts Combs has secured behind bars.

"He’s a billionaire. People are in awe of him," one of the anonymous sources told the outlet. "Money is power, especially behind bars."

DIDDY SENT TO SOLITARY CONFINEMENT AFTER PRISON FIGHT WITH ANOTHER INMATE: MULTIPLE REPORTS

From freshly made beds to cooked meals, clean laundry and Chinese-style massages, Diddy has reportedly turned fellow inmates into a makeshift prison staff.

"This is not some normal s--- you see in jail. This is some rich s---," one of the men told NBC. "It looks crazy, but again, it’s Diddy."

Contraband cellphones, explicit photos, prescription pills and premium booze — Combs’ alleged prison perks reportedly extend well beyond his makeshift staff.

Sources told NBC News the music mogul uses illicit phones to scroll Instagram and view nude and sexually explicit photos sent by an ex-girlfriend. He has also allegedly purchased Remeron, an antidepressant dubbed "rem-roms" behind bars, from other inmates for its mood-boosting effects.

On weekend nights, Combs would reportedly break into a secret stash of top-shelf liquor allegedly smuggled into the prison by guards and shared with a small circle of inmates.

"You can pretty much get anything except a key to the front door and a female," one of the sources said.

Diddy had even gotten his hands on a "jailbroken" tablet to watch movies – including "Sean Combs: The Reckoning," produced by 50 Cent – according to the men.

LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS

Combs’ representative pushed back on the portrayal of his life behind bars, dismissing the attention surrounding his day-to-day routine as overblown.

"The continued scrutiny of every mundane detail of Sean Combs’s life in prison has reached the point where the media characterizes ordinary prison life as news," Diddy's rep told Fox News Digital. "The only real news is that Sean continues to serve his sentence within the rules, and he patiently awaits the court’s decision on his appeal."

PUT YOUR ENTERTAINMENT KNOWLEDGE TO THE TEST AND SEE HOW YOU SCORE

In response to the reported claims involving contraband cellphones, drugs and alcohol, FCI Fort Dix acknowledged that keeping prohibited items out of federal prisons remains an ongoing challenge.

"Like all correctional agencies, contraband, particularly cell phones, narcotics, and weapons, remains a constant challenge, and we continue to tackle the problem of contraband being introduced into our facilities," a representative for FCI Fort Dix told Fox News Digital. "Inmates are not permitted to have access to cell phones, and all incarcerated individuals in the Federal Bureau of Prisons (BOP) who are found to violate the ‘Inmate Discipline Program’ policy are subject to sanctions."

"We are fully committed to safeguarding everyone in our custody and to maintaining the safety and security of our correctional staff and surrounding communities," the statement continued. "To this end, we operate under a controlled environment that is both secure and humane. Additionally, based on the need to ensure safety and security in our institutions and in accordance with privacy concerns, we do not discuss potential allegations of staff misconduct, nor do we confirm or deny the existence of a corresponding investigation."

"However, we generally can tell you that allegations of staff misconduct are taken seriously and, consistent with national policy, referred for investigation if warranted," the statement concluded. "Incidents of potential criminal activity or misconduct inside BOP facilities are thoroughly investigated for potential administrative discipline or criminal prosecution."

The musician was sentenced on Oct. 3, 2025 to 50 months behind bars, followed by five years of supervised release and a $500,000 fine. The rapper was transferred to Fort Dix to serve out the rest of his sentence later that month. As of publication, Diddy's release date was set as Jan. 21, 2028.

Diddy's eight-week trial, during which jurors heard dozens of witness testimonies, concluded on July 2, 2025. The rapper was acquitted on the most serious charges against him – sex-trafficking and racketeering.

The "I'll Be Missing You" singer has filed an appeal. Diddy's team claimed the sentence handed down to him was illegal because the judge relied on charges the jury rejected, according to the appeal briefing obtained by Fox News Digital.

item.title: Enes Kanter Freedom speaks out on A'ja Wilson playoff incident with Fever fan, after Natasha Cloud encounter
item.description: Enes Kanter Freedom says the WNBA should suspend the Las Vegas Aces star after she left the court to confront an Indiana Fever fan in the playoffs.
item.content:encoded:
Former NBA player Enes Kanter Freedom called on the WNBA to suspend Las Vegas Aces star A’ja Wilson after she confronted an Indiana Fever fan during Tuesday’s playoff game.

Wilson received a technical foul after leaving the court and approaching the spectator during the fourth quarter of Indiana’s 99-89 victory at Gainbridge Fieldhouse. The fan had stood, pointed toward Wilson and appeared to blame her for a foul called on Fever guard Sophie Cunningham.

"I think A’ja Wilson should be suspended," Freedom told OutKick. "The league should hold her accountable because the fans are the ones that are paying the salaries of these players. As a player, they need to respect fans more."

ACES' A'JA WILSON GETS TECH FOR CONFRONTATION WITH FEVER FAN, WHO WAS DETERMINED TO HAVE BROKEN NO RULES

Freedom also defended the fan, after he was the subject of scrutiny on social media and in the broadcast booth.

"Listen, he did not do anything wrong," Freedom said. "He was just very passionate about the game."

The Fever said arena security interviewed the fan and witnesses and found no violation of the WNBA Fan Code of Conduct.

"Following a report of a comment directed toward a player, arena security spoke with the fan involved and witnesses," the team said. "Security determined there was no violation of the Fan Code of Conduct, the fan was not removed from the arena. We consider the matter closed."

The man was escorted away from his seat temporarily but was later allowed to return.

Freedom argued Wilson should have been ejected under Rule 12A, Section V of the WNBA rulebook, which says any player, coach, trainer or other team bench member who deliberately enters the spectator stands during a game will be automatically ejected. The rule also defines the first row of seats as the beginning of the stands. Wilson instead received only a technical foul.

ENES KANTER FREEDOM SENDS LETTER TO WNBA REQUESTING REVIEW OF SKY EJECTION INCIDENT, FULL TICKET REFUND

"The rules are very simple and very clear," Freedom said. "If the fan stepped on the court, he would be thrown out immediately. I think the same rules apply for players as well.

"If the player steps off the court and walks toward the fans and then starts yelling and screaming, I think she should be thrown out immediately. So I think Cathy Engelbert has a tough decision to make. But I think she should be suspended for the next game."

Freedom said the incident reminded him of his own confrontation with Chicago Sky guard Natasha Cloud in August. Freedom was removed from Wintrust Arena and later banned from Sky home games after he stood from his courtside seat and took a step toward the court while exchanging words with Cloud.

"It’s the same situation," Freedom said of Wilson’s confrontation. "I saw the fan. He simply got up, pointed at her, and then she just lost her mind. It was a lot of emotions, and then she was yelling and screaming.

"The same thing happened to me. I simply got up, put my hands up in the air, and then Natasha Cloud was barking at me."

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

Sky principal owner Michael Alter told OutKick that Freedom became a "potential threat" when he took the step. Freedom has since filed a federal lawsuit against the Sky, the Metropolitan Pier and Exposition Authority and the City of Chicago, alleging he was ejected and banned because of his speech and viewpoint. The defendants have disputed Freedom’s account.

In terms of Tuesday's incident, Wilson offered a different assessment after the game, saying she believed the fan had stepped toward her in an unacceptable manner.

"If I’m just walking because I got the foul and I’m just chilling, and if I see a man coming at me, taking steps toward me, pointing at me, I don’t give a damn what you said," Wilson said. "I don’t give a damn how you said it, the tone, that is unacceptable. You don’t step towards me, you never point at me, that’s unacceptable."

Wilson apologized to her teammates for receiving the technical foul but stood by her response to the fan. Aces coach Becky Hammon said she did not see the entire exchange but defended Wilson, saying she had never seen the four-time MVP react that way and believed Wilson felt "very disrespected."

Freedom acknowledged Wilson’s status as one of the league’s premier players while arguing it should bring a greater responsibility to control her reaction.

"A’ja Wilson is the face of the league," he said. "She is definitely one of the top two or three players, and I do respect her a lot. Obviously, she’s going to be a Hall of Famer. But as someone who’s the face of the league, she definitely needs to control her emotions."

Freedom, who has made opposition to biological males competing in women’s sports a central part of his recent activism, said he is rooting for Indiana in the series.

"I just hope that they win because the more they win, the more spotlight is going to be on the question of whether they can even define what a woman is," he said.

Indiana’s victory evened the best-of-three first-round series at one game apiece. Caitlin Clark finished with 27 points, 15 assists and seven rebounds, while Wilson had 22 points and nine rebounds. The decisive Game 3 is scheduled for Thursday night in Las Vegas.

Freedom said he was considering attending the game but had not finalized his plans because of a previously scheduled rally.

"It will be interesting to see what the WNBA comes up with," he said. "If they suspend her, I will definitely go and cheer for Indiana. Even if they don’t suspend her, it would be nice to go and see what kind of reaction all the fans and all the players are getting."

However, Freedom did reveal that he is planning to be in attendance for Game 1 of the WNBA Finals on Oct. 17, whichever teams are involved.

"I'm definitely planning to go to WNBA Finals Game 1."

item.title: Trump Pentagon launches competition for America's next great military base
item.description: The winning state for the base site will be selected through a merit-based competition based on land, housing, schools, community support and regulatory cooperation.
item.content:encoded:
Secretary of War Pete Hegseth on Wednesday announced plans to build a modern, self-sustaining military fortress, saying the site will be selected through a merit-based competition among governors pitching their states as potential locations.

The megaproject, dubbed the "Next Great American Base," was unveiled during an address at Marine Corps Base Quantico as part of Hegseth’s six strategies to modernize the military.

The initiative rejects what Hegseth described as the legacy approach to spend heavily on advanced weapons systems while service members live on aging bases with outdated barracks.

"For too long, our military has been bogged down by the same old tired Washington playbook: spending trillions on exquisite weapons systems, while our troops live in aging bases, outdated barracks, and with inadequate infrastructure. That era is over," Hegseth said.

EXCLUSIVE: HEGSETH TO DOUBLE CUTS TO GENERALS, ADMIRALS IN MAJOR PENTAGON SHAKEUP

"To back up our warfighters, when we bring the troops home, we won’t just reshuffle troops onto legacy posts. We are going to build them beautiful new bases from the ground up," he added.

The ambitious undertaking will feature a brand-new military installation spanning hundreds of thousands of acres and housing up to 25,000 service members.

"We are talking hundreds of thousands of acres with organic power generation, modern air defenses, and cutting edge technology — a fortress," he said.

The installation is expected to provide first-class living conditions, high-end training grounds and essential services such as health care and child care, while operating entirely off the commercial grid with independent power sources.

Hegseth added that the base will support President Donald Trump’s executive order on "Beautiful Civic Architecture," which calls for federal public buildings and military installations to be designed in timeless and classical styles.

"We owe our warriors nothing less than the gold standard," Hegseth said.

SENATE REPUBLICAN PUSHES MERIT-BASED MILITARY PROMOTIONS, TARGETS BIDEN-ERA DEI POLICIES

To determine the site location, the Department of War said it is launching a transparent, merit-based competition in which state governors can pitch their proposals directly to top military leadership at the Pentagon.

The winning state will be chosen based on its ability to remove regulatory hurdles and bureaucracy to speed up construction, while offering the best package of land, community support, top-tier housing, schools and other services.

"The state that cuts the most red tape and offers the best package of land and support will win the historic honor of hosting the most lethal, modern, and beautiful military installation on the planet," a press release stated.

Pitch deliberations will be recorded and made public to eliminate "political favoritism," according to the Pentagon.

"No backroom Washington deals. No political favoritism – just a straight-up, merit-based contest to see which state will partner with us to build the most modern, beautiful, and lethal military installation on the planet," Hegseth said.

The project is the fourth announcement among six major strategic initiatives unveiled by the secretary.

According to the Department of War, the other initiatives focus on restoring male physical standards and combat roles, improving the comprehensive review of military standards, overhauling complaint processes, reforming senior leadership and focusing on core training and maintenance.

item.title: Caitlin Clark puking her brains out at halftime appears to be key to Indiana Fever victories
item.description: Caitlin Clark revealed she threw up at halftime of the Indiana Fever's Game 2 win over the Aces, and the star is now 2-0 after midgame vomiting.
item.content:encoded:
All of the focus after Game 2 between the Indiana Fever and the Las Vegas Aces was on A'ja Wilson getting into it with a fan. That's a shame because it overshadowed a gutsy — in every sense — postseason performance from Caitlin Clark.

The Fever kept the best-of-three series alive with a 99-88 win, and in it Clark posted 27 points, 15 assists and seven rebounds.

And she did it all despite going all Old Faithful in the team's locker room at halftime.

ZERO BS. JUST DAKICH. TAKE THE DON'T @ ME PODCAST ON THE ROAD. DOWNLOAD NOW!

"To be honest, I threw up everything in my stomach at halftime," Clark said after the game. "I was just out there so tired. It wasn’t because I didn’t feel good or anything. I just was that gassed."

Way to power through it. For some reason, puking is exhausting. Most of us puke and then cancel plans; Clark went out there and continued to ball.

But what's wild is that this has happened to Clark before.

And, even wilder, the Fever are 2-0 if she gets an encore presentation from her pregame meal.

PRIME VIDEO WNBA BROADCAST CREW EMBARRASSES ITSELF WITH COVERAGE OF A'JA WILSON FAN INCIDENT

In June, Clark vomited at halftime during a game against the Atlanta Dream, which the Fever went on to win.

So, with the season on the line, the team might need to make sure she takes a beeline to a prayer session with the porcelain god next game.

If I were head coach Stephanie White, I’d say, "All right, ladies, pregame meal at the raw bar down the street. The team nutritionist will make recommendations, but Caitlin, I’ve already entered you in the three-dozen oyster challenge. Finish them and you get a T-shirt. That's team building!"

Then after she housed thirty-six mollusks and earned herself a very thin, XL shirt, we'd hit Baskin-Robbins for samples of as many of their 31 flavors as possible before heading back to Gainbridge Fieldhouse.

There, I'd tell Clark to relax in the steam room for a bit, and when she's done — what do you know? — it'd be time for a pregame warm-up jog.

That should create a maelstrom in the ol' tummy, but if not, I'd have some pimple-popping videos cued up on a TV in the locker room at the half just as a fail-safe measure.

That seems a bit much, but you can't argue with statistics: Clark puking means a win.

And that's what the Fever need when they head to Vegas for Game 3 on Thursday night.

item.title: The best hiking and outdoor spots near Folsom Field for Texas Tech at Colorado game weekend
item.description: Texas Tech arrives in Boulder undefeated and ranked No. 12 to face Colorado at Folsom Field, but the real draw may be the trails surrounding campus.
item.content:encoded:
Week 5 | Texas Tech at Colorado | Saturday, Oct. 3 | Folsom Field, Boulder, CO | 7:30 PM ET | FOX

OK, let's not pretend this is a marquee matchup on paper.

Colorado stumbled out of its Big 12 opener with a 23-13 loss to Baylor, dropping Coach Prime's Buffaloes to 2-2 and looking like (potentially) the worst team in the conference. That's on the heels of a 41-7 blowout at Northwestern that was ugly enough for Deion Sanders to dismiss a handful of players for conduct detrimental to the team days later.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE COVERAGE FROM OUTKICK OUTDOORS

Texas Tech, meanwhile, rolls into Boulder undefeated at 4-0, ranked No. 12, and looking every bit like the defending Big 12 champs they are.

So no, the Buffaloes probably aren't pulling off the upset. But the vibes in Boulder remain immaculate, and this might be the single best outdoor city on the entire schedule this season.

6 OF THE BEST FALL CAMPING DESTINATIONS IN AMERICA, PLUS GEAR BEGINNERS SHOULD PACK

Whatever happens at Folsom Field, fans in town for the game still get to enjoy some of the best terrain in the country.

Under 10 minutes from Folsom Field | Easy to strenuous

The single best trailhead in Boulder, and it's basically in town. Options range from the easy 1.3-mile Chautauqua Trail loop to the legendary Royal Arch hike — 3.3 miles, steep, a 4.8-star rating from over 20,000 AllTrails reviews, ending at a natural stone arch overlooking the city. If your group has wildly different fitness levels, this is the one trailhead that can handle all of them at once.

Walkable from Folsom Field | Easy

Runs right through downtown, so there's no real "drive time" to speak of. Rent a bike from University Bikes or B-Cycle and ride the paved path, or just walk down and watch people tube, fish and wade in the creek itself. The lowest-effort option on this list.

About 20 minutes from Folsom Field | $10-12 per vehicle | Moderate to strenuous

Boulder's rock-climbing mecca, and a legitimately beautiful canyon even if you're not the one climbing. The Eldorado Canyon Trail is a 6.8-mile out-and-back along South Boulder Creek, 4.7 stars, with towering sandstone walls the whole way.

Minutes west of downtown | Easy to moderate

The free alternative to Eldorado, running along the same corridor. Climbing, fishing and creekside scenery without the entrance fee — a good pick if you'd rather not pay to park.

About an hour from Folsom Field | Entrance fee applies | Varies

The obvious star of the show.

This one runs a little past our usual drive-time window for game day, but c'mon — it's Rocky Mountain National Park. Just don't try to squeeze it into a pregame window. Between the drive and the sheer size of the park, this isn't a two-hour detour before kickoff. It's a half-day minimum, and honestly a full day if you want to do it right.

If you're only in Boulder for the game itself, save this one for another trip. But if you're turning the weekend into a longer stay, or tacking on an extra day before or after, this is exactly where you want to be.

Heads up: Between late May and mid-October, driving into RMNP during peak hours (9 a.m. - 2 p.m. for general park access, or 5 a.m. - 6 p.m. for the Bear Lake Road corridor) requires a Timed Entry Permit reserved in advance on Recreation.gov ($2 reservation fee) in addition to the standard entrance fee.

item.title: Cheapest Costco prepared meal costs shockingly little per serving: 'Can't beat the price'
item.description: Kirkland Signature Mac and Cheese from Costco ranks as the cheapest prepared deli meal per serving, while rotisserie chicken Asian wraps top the price list.
item.content:encoded:
Costco shoppers aiming to stretch their dollars may want to take a closer look at the club's prepared meals.

A new report from the food site Tasting Table estimated which Kirkland Signature deli favorites cost the most and least per serving. The outlet estimated the cost per serving using Denver-area prices, estimated package weights and the serving sizes listed on nutrition labels.

Based on those estimates, Costco's Kirkland Signature Mac and Cheese offered the lowest estimated cost per serving, the outlet found, while the Kirkland Signature Rotisserie Chicken Asian Wrap with Dressing ranked as the most expensive among the meals it analyzed.

SAM'S CLUB MEAL KIT FEEDS A FAMILY FOR UNDER $16 AS SHOPPERS SEEK AFFORDABLE DINNERS

A tray of the mac and cheese costs about $4.53 per pound in the Denver area and weighs an estimated 3.76 pounds for a total of roughly $17 per tray, or about $1.42 per serving. 

The nutrition label lists about 12 servings per container.

On the other end of the spectrum, the wraps sell for about $7.93 per pound, with an estimated package weight of 2.38 pounds, which works out to about $4.72 per serving. 

Each package contains four wraps, which the publication counted as four servings.

COSTCO SHOPPERS DIVIDED OVER NEW 'SOURDOUGH' BREAD AS CRITICS SAY IT'S NOT THE REAL THING

The analysis was based on one regional market and estimated package weights, which can vary because Costco's prepared deli meals are sold by weight. 

Prices and availability may also differ by warehouse.

Tasting Table did not specify whether it evaluated every Kirkland Signature prepared meal or if it identified all the products included in its comparison. 

It also noted that nutrition label serving sizes may not reflect how much customers actually eat in a single sitting.

COSTCO FOOD COURT ITEM PACKS MORE PROTEIN THAN ANYTHING ELSE ON THE MENU, BUT THERE'S A CATCH

In a Reddit community dedicated to mac and cheese, users debated the Kirkland Signature offering. 

Despite being among the cheapest ready-made options, according to Tasting Table, one user said, "Never found these to be worth the cost."

Another person, however, called the mac and cheese "better than 90% of the ready-made out there," while others suggested adding breadcrumbs, bacon or extra seasoning.

In a Reddit forum dedicated to Costco, users were also split over the wraps.

Some raved over the dressing used on them and their convenience, while others criticized them as "super bland" and said they weren't impressed.

Toshie Lucas, a Texas-based content creator who posts online as @costcotv, said she wasn't surprised by the results.

"The mac and cheese is so delicious, and our kids love it," Lucas told Fox News Digital. "You really can't beat the price for how much you get."

CLICK HERE FOR MORE LIFESTYLE STORIES

Of the wraps, Lucas said, "They're good to grab for an easy lunch ... but that's pretty expensive for a wrap, in my opinion."

TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

Lucas added that shoppers should weigh factors beyond price, including leftover potential, convenience and whether their family — especially kids — will actually eat the meal.

"Sometimes paying a little more is worth it when you need something quick for the family," she noted.

item.title: Unearthed clip exposes the Talarico comment that triggered backlash from parents
item.description: James Talarico, the Democratic Texas U.S. Senate candidate, dismissed parents' concerns about pornography in schools as a "conspiracy theory" at a 2022 hearing.
item.content:encoded:
James Talarico, the Democratic candidate for U.S. Senate in Texas, once dismissed public outcry about explicit material in Texas public schools as a kind of "conspiracy theory" at a July 2022 hearing on education.

"We’re going to spend hours hearing bills that are just kind of conspiracy theory-driven and kind of kooky stuff. And we’re going to hear some of that today, I think, in the public testimony — not the invited testimony, but the public testimony," Talarico said then as a member of the Texas House of Representatives.

The resurfaced moment adds to the pile of past statements dealing with gender, immigration and law enforcement, complicating the political calculus for Talarico as he aims to convince voters in Texas that, even as a Democrat, he could represent a Republican-leaning constituency in the Lone Star State.

TED CRUZ, CONSERVATIVES RESPOND AFTER TALARICO CRITICIZES BIBLE-RELATED EDUCATION IN SCHOOLS AS 'PROPAGANDA'

At the time of the 2022 hearing, many parents were raising concerns about news that schools and libraries across the country were featuring explicit materials that bordered on pornography. 

In particular, an Ashland, Ohio, board meeting made news after a group of angry parents highlighted graphic illustrations from books like "It’s Perfectly Normal," "Making a Baby," "Own Your Period" and "Puberty is Gross but Also Really Awesome," all titles featuring some level of sexual references.

Similar outcries emerged in Kentucky, Oregon and North Carolina.

In Texas, state Rep. Matt Krause, a Republican, sparked similar backlash when he circulated a list of roughly 800 titles he believed were inappropriate for students. He expressed his alarm in a letter to Texas school districts.

"I am writing to you as the Chairman of the Texas House Committee on General Investigation," Krause wrote. "The committee may initiate inquiries concerning any ‘matter the committee considers necessary for the information of the legislature or for the welfare and protection of state citizens.’

"Please identify any other books or content in your district, specifying the campus location and funds spent on acquisition that address or contain … sexually explicit images, graphic presentations of sexual behavior that is in violation of the law or contain material that might make students feel discomfort, guilt, anguish or any other form of psychological distress because of their race or sex or convey that a student, by virtue of their race or sex is inherently racist sexist or oppressive whether consciously or unconsciously."

CONTROVERSIAL TEACHER TRAINING TARGETS PARENTAL AUTHORITY AS OPPRESSION, EDUCATION EXPERT WARNS

In January 2022, several counties began evaluating their own books, leading some, like Granbury Independent School District, to pull 130 titles from shelves.

By July, the issue had made its way before the Texas Legislature in the form of an "interim charge," made by Republican Texas House Speaker Dade Phelan. It was a kind of exhortation for lawmakers to examine the issue, charging them to "monitor and analyze the state policy on curriculum and instructional materials used in public schools."

As a part of the Committee on Public Education, Talarico received the charge but expressed reservations about its substance, making his "conspiracy theory" comment.

He went on to ask Texas Education Agency Commissioner Mike Morath about the issue.

"I want to ask you about curriculum in Texas, of course, critical race theory, pornography; these are the things we see bubbling up on social media that’s going to be discussed here," Talarico said.

"Are you aware of any curriculum in the state of Texas that, one, bullies students based on their race or, two, grooms students with pornography?"

Morath, after noting that Texas is a very big state and the issue is "very complex," gave his blunt assessment.

"The answer is yes," Morath said.

"We have complaints that would appear to substantiate periodic problems in those areas, arguably. I can’t tell you it’s widespread. We’ve reviewed, in some cases, materials that were made available to students that I think the common citizen would agree would be inappropriate."

CARVILLE ADVISES TALARICO 'TO DEAL WITH' PAST CULTURE WAR COMMENTS IF HE WANTS TO WIN TEXAS

Even after the testimony, Talarico challenged the idea that explicit materials in schools were widespread.

"I would characterize as a conspiracy theory that’s being raised is that these are systemic policy problems in the state of Texas," Talarico said.

Following Talarico’s remarks, parents spoke out against his characterization.

"I actually drove in last night, so I’ve been here a very long time. And hopefully my comments and testimony today aren’t gonna be as ‘kooky’ as Representative Talarico had stated it was gonna be," one parent quipped.

Talarico’s campaign did not immediately respond to a request for comment from Fox News Digital.

item.title: GOP challenger tears into Dem's 'moderate' image: 'Votes with the squad 90% of the time'
item.description: Scott Singer, GOP candidate in FL-25, denounces Democrat incumbent Rep. Jared Moskowitz's voting record, alliance with "the squad," and calls into question his support for Israel.
item.content:encoded:
Republican congressional candidate Scott Singer is making the case that party, not just policy, will be decisive in his closely watched South Florida showdown with Democrat Rep. Jared Moskowitz, arguing that the incumbent’s moderate, pro-Israel image is at odds with his voting record and the direction of the Democrat Party.

Singer, the former mayor of Boca Raton, told Fox News Digital that he believes his record of cutting taxes and reducing crime at the local level, combined with unwavering support for Israel, gives voters a clear contrast in Florida’s newly redrawn 25th Congressional District.

"Well, it is a tough cycle, but people understand the real Jared Moskowitz, one who votes with the squad 90% of the time, voted to put [Rep.] Ilhan Omar [D-Minn.] on the Foreign Affairs Committee, has passed no bills in Congress, but traded $4.5 million worth of stocks since he's been there. This district, after redistricting, is now a Republican plus five district," Singer told Fox News Digital.  

GOP'S SINGER 'VERY PREPARED' TO OUST DEM MOSKOWITZ IN TOSS-UP FLORIDA RACE THAT COULD DETERMINE HOUSE MAJORITY

"It takes in all of Boca Raton, where I was mayor for eight years, cut taxes, red tape, and crime, and goes down to Miami Beach, where I was born, and Fort Lauderdale, where I was raised," he continued. "Moskowitz doesn't live in the district, he's not from the district. 

"But beyond that, the Republican plus five, a trend in Jewish voters, of which we have 25% … in our district, moving more conservatively, and people who are opposed to socialism and communism, which he will not denounce, understand that this is a critical race for House leadership, and they want someone like me, a local leader with a record of results." 

Singer's business-friendly fiscal conservatism is the cornerstone of his campaign, and provides the policy framework for his priorities on Capitol Hill.

"Well, it gives me the record of results one would need. As mayor of Boca Raton, not only did we have the lowest property tax rate of any full-service city in Florida, I cut the tax rate seven times. I cut red tape, 21 streamlining initiatives," he said. "I cut crime by more than 25% from what were 40-year lows. Those are a record of results that people can relate to, because we improved the quality of life, improved the job base, lowered taxes, and made our streets safer."

UNEARTHED AUDIT EXPOSES VULNERABLE DEM'S HANDLING OF COVID RELIEF FUNDS: 'GROSS OVERSIGHT'

Singer continued: "That's what we want right now in America. We want secure borders, not like the porous borders that Jared Moskowitz supported under [former] President [Joe] Biden that have increased crime and ravaged communities. They want tax relief, not the tax hike that he voted for. $4 trillion, including taxes on Social Security, tipped workers, small businesses and families that are hurting. Now he's trying to come around with a modest talk of the gas tax reduction. 

"He had the chance to vote on taxes and repeatedly has voted for higher taxes. People want a leader with a record of results. That's what I bring."

While Moskowitz has carefully cultivated a moderate image during his tenure in Congress, Singer disputes that characterization. 

"No, he's not. He's been voting in lockstep. He's already said he'll vote for whoever the Democratic leadership is. And you can see that we'll have committee chairs like [Rep.] Rashida Tlaib [D-Mich.] and AOC [Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, D-N.Y.], if heaven forbid, the Democrats win Congress," Singer said. "He already voted for Ilhan Omar on Foreign Affairs, despite his talking about her statements being bad, he voted to keep her in charge of foreign affairs in our country." 

FLORIDA GOP NOMINEE BLASTS 20-YEAR DEM INCUMBENT AS A ‘SOCIALIST’ RUBBER-STAMP WITH ‘PRECIOUS LITTLE TO SHOW’

Added Singer: "He's voted for tax hikes again … He says he's strong on Israel, but he voted against US-Israeli cooperation, when other Democrats were willing to cross the aisle. And then just a few weeks ago, he would not denounce socialism, even though other Democrats would. He's trying to have it out both ways, but his record is really Democratic, really liberal, 90% with the squad."

Both Moskowitz and Singer both position themselves as strong supporters of Israel, but Singer argues that membership in today's Democrat Party makes effective advocacy for Israel difficult.

"I'm a stronger supporter for Israel. I would never have put Ilhan Omar on the Foreign Affairs Committee. I would not have, like he did, voted against U.S.-Israel cooperation in the NDAA [National Defense Authorization Act]," Singer said. "I would have not voted to undercut President [Donald] Trump's efforts and our military's efforts with the War Powers Act vote months ago when the U.S. and Israel were fighting against a common enemy. 

"He's done all of those things because Democratic leadership requires him. And he admitted three weeks ago to Jewish Insider that he's being ostracized in his own party. He doesn't have any more chits to give in. He has to go with the way the majority is going, and that expanded squad is going to tamp out any voice he has. 

"In my party, support for Israel is a feature, not a bug, and I don't have to moderate my views or vote in accordance with the majority…I can be a strong supporter for Israel without reservation. Jared's admitted he can't be and won't be."

Finally, while Singer said he is a strong supporter of the Trump administration's military engagement in Iran, he would like to see an end to the conflict soon.

"I think we need to have a resolution of this. I think we need to emerge victoriously. We have to remember that nuclear Iran is an existential threat," he said. "We have seen how dastardly, vicious, murderous this regime has been over 47 years. Their foreign policy is death to America. They've killed Americans, they'll kill more. 

"And even since this conflict started, they've started attacking other nations who weren't combatants trying to widen the conflict. They support terror across the world. It's hurt America, it's hurt Americans, it's hurt our allies like Israel, and it's hurting the free world. We need to stop this. 

"And I am optimistic we'll see a resolution soon. And that's a small price to pay. Even if we have some hiccups there, it's a smaller price to pay to ensure Iran does not have a nuclear weapon."

item.title: Sophie Cunningham sends message after pathetic finger-pointing tantrum & Sox-Yanks announcers won't shut up!
item.description: Sophie Cunningham used TikTok to call out the WNBA rulebook after a player entered the stands to confront a fan in Indiana without being ejected.
item.content:encoded:
'Nightcaps' is a daily column that catches you up on the biggest sports, news and culture stories you may have missed while pretending to do work at your desk. It runs Monday-Friday on OutKick.com.

I don't know what's worse ...

My Red Sox getting absolutely embarrassed in Game 1 against the Yankees, or the fact that we still have WNBA drama to parse through on the final day of September.

Thank goodness for Sophie Cunningham. At least we can work her into today's class after last night's debacle in Indy. She's a content machine, and, frankly, makes a good point about the WNBA and the rules.

ACES' A'JA WILSON GETS TECH FOR CONFRONTATION WITH FEVER FAN, WHO WAS DETERMINED TO HAVE BROKEN NO RULES

You'll see.

But first ... welcome to a Hump Day Nightcaps — the one where Sophie sends the league a message via her TikTok account. Nobody is doing it quite like Sophie right now. She's at the absolute top of her game ... off the court, at least. I'd like to see a few more baskets on the court, but that's just being nitpicky.

What else should we hit on today? My Red Sox looked like trash last night, and I'm not sure it's getting any better tonight. The days of 2004 (and '07, '13 and '18) are long gone. Sad.

I've also got a USC announcer offering up a sizzling take on the dirtiest hit in college football from last weekend, Mario Lopez using just the wildest AI image of Mr. Belding I've ever seen after news of his death broke yesterday and I need to ask you guys about these NBC/Peacock MLB broadcasts.

Is it just me, or do these guys not shut up? I couldn't take it last night. I felt like I was listening to a three-hour podcast during Sox-Yanks, and the game was nothing more than background noise. It was stunning.

OK, grab you one final September drink before the greatest month of the year begins tomorrow, and settle in for a Hump Day 'Cap!

Look, I don't want to do much WNBA today. I don't have it in me. It's football season. It's the MLB postseason. Hockey started yesterday. I spent all summer doing this, and I was hoping to move on ...

But the girls just refuse to give up the news cycle!

DETAILS EMERGE IN INCIDENT BETWEEN ACES STAR A'JA WILSON AND FEVER FAN DURING PLAYOFF GAME

"You're the one who writes about it! Stop covering it, and they'll stop being relevant!"

Yes, I know. I've heard it before. My job is to follow the content. And last night, the content was in Indiana, where A’ja Wilson threw a tantrum because a fan ...

Well, the fan did nothing wrong. Literally. He simply pointed at her after she got tangled up with Sophie Cunningham, resulting in a foul.

Wilson took it so personally, that she actually went into the stands to confront this VERY MEAN FAN. She didn't quite make it to him, but she still entered the stands.

That, according to the pesky WNBA rulebook, ain't allowed. It comes with an automatic ejection, and triggers an investigation from the league. None of that happened.

So, being the only sane player in the league, Cunningham took it upon herself to raise that exact point in a social media post Wednesday afternoon.

"Not trying to be dramatic at all, but I'm just here trying to have my morning coffee and, what a damn comeback year for the point," Cunningham said in the post, which was simply captioned "According to the rulebook....."

Amazing. She never misses ... like I said, off the court.

Cunningham, of course, went viral over the summer when she antagonized an opposing player by simply pointing at her. The clip exploded, T-shirts were made and Sophie's stardom took off like a rocket ship.

Cunningham wasn't ejected or fined or anything like that, but that's because she didn't do anything wrong. According to the WNBA rules, Wilson did. And the league has, so far, looked the other way.

Rules are for thee!

OK, that's enough WNBA talk for today. We've got more playoff baseball on deck, with four more games this afternoon and tonight. Same schedule as yesterday. Same announcers.

And that's just terrible news for Sox and Yankees fans ...

I could go on and on. It was unbearable.

Anthony Rizzo? Stinks. Joe Girardi? Nails on a chalkboard. Lou Merloni? Actually good, but couldn't get a word in because Girardi and Rizzo, two former YANKEES, wouldn't shut up.

Why do we suddenly need these 3, 4 and 5-man broadcast booths? I don't get it. We went decades — decades! — with two-man booths. And now the big thing is to stuff as many people in the booth as humanly possible, and have them constantly talk the whole game? I don't get it.

God, I miss Buck and McCarver. We had it so good, and we pissed it away.

Sad.

OK, let's rapid-fire this Hump Day class into a big Hump Day night. First up? While we're on the topic of broadcast booths, let's go ahead and check in with the USC fellas after last weekend's disgusting late hit that sent Dante Moore to the ER:

"He did not try to slide feet first. Stephens went in helmet-first, but he kind of ran into Dante Moore, who ducked into that hit. I did not see him put his feet out first. I saw him dive forward."

Amazing. What a sequence. What analysis by USC play-by-play man, Pete Arbogast. I've never seen anything like it. Just stunning.

Even when the rest of the crew told Arbogast that Moore did, indeed, slide feet first, he offered this bit of incredible spin.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

"Well he is now because they spun him around," he said before looking at the replay and coming to his final conclusion. "Well, he goes into, not a feet-first slide, more of a knee-slide. It didn't look like targeting on the replay to us."

Yep. No targeting there, Pete! Just good, clean football. Textbook stuff, really.

Next? Speaking of textbook stuff, how about this AI picture of Mr. Belding that Mario Lopez posted yesterday, just hours after Dennis Haskins' death?

Can you spot the issue?!

Incredible. How does one see that, and think to themself, "Yeah, this is it. This is the one!" What a move here by AC Slater. Poor Mr. Belding.

PS: I'm super bummed Dennis Haskins died. He was our childhood. Him and Bob Saget. And now, we've lost both.

Brutal.

OK, that's it for today — and this month! We did it. We're into October, boys and girls. Soak it all up.

Let's say one final goodbye to summer with NASCAR's Natalie Decker, and start this new month with a bang.

See you tomorrow.

Did you watch the Sox-Yanks game and notice the nonstop yapping? Zach.Dean@OutKick.com.
